# Guest Artist Office Handbook

Fictional Cedar Lantern Dance Studio. Training fixture only; no real studio policy.

## Booking a visiting teacher
The guest office manages visiting artists who teach a short residency without joining the regular teaching rota. A guest session is attached to a named host teacher and a named room. The host remains responsible for the register, emergency information and closing the room; artistic leadership does not transfer these duties. An invitation email is an expression of interest until the guest office issues a numbered booking confirmation. Students must not infer a confirmed visit from a social post or a poster left over from a previous residency.

The guest office requires a visiting artist booking request at least 18 calendar days before the first workshop. A request records the teaching theme, room, age band, planned equipment and whether an observer will attend. Count the first teaching day as day zero. A request received on a weekend still receives its actual received date, but no appointment is held open while missing details are collected. The office offers a written alternative date when the requested lead time cannot be met.

## Changing a confirmed workshop
A confirmed guest workshop may be moved once without an administration fee if the host gives seven full days of notice. The change must retain the same visiting teacher and cohort. Replacing the guest, changing an adult class into a youth class, or adding a second day is a new booking request. A room change requested by building staff does not consume the host's one permitted move. The host sends the new room confirmation directly to enrolled participants and keeps the old message in the office record.

When a visiting artist cancels, the office offers either a replacement workshop or a full workshop-fee refund within ten business days. The office records each participant's choice. A regular class credit is not substituted without the participant's express choice. The ordinary timetable continues unless the host sends a separate message explaining an alteration; a cancelled guest event does not cancel an entire term of tuition.

## Booking payment and competing handout
The office handbook sets the guest-workshop reservation deposit at 35 dollars per participant. A receipt identifies the workshop booking number and payment date. The office is aware that the artist welcome handout prints a different deposit amount for the same workshops; both documents remain current and no precedence instruction has been issued. Staff must surface the discrepancy for a human decision rather than choosing the larger, smaller or newer-looking figure. Do not add the two deposits together. An archived flyer for a community concert has a separate 12 dollar entry contribution and is not a guest-workshop deposit.

## Observation and access to rehearsal
A visiting teacher may invite a colleague to observe from the marked bench. Observation has no teaching entitlement. The colleague cannot join a youth exercise, photograph participants or take attendance merely because the guest invited them. The host records the visitor's arrival and explains the exits. A late observer waits until the next natural break rather than crossing the dance floor during a sequence.

Every guest workshop containing any participant under 16 must have a rostered studio host present throughout the teaching period. This condition also applies to one-to-one coaching. A remote host available by telephone does not count as present. If the host must leave the building, teaching pauses until another rostered host takes over; the guest cannot waive this requirement.

## Files, expenses and travel
A guest supplies their public teaching biography as plain text. The office checks spelling before copying it to a studio event listing. Passport scans and bank details are collected through the private administration channel and never placed in the workshop plan. The booking number is sufficient in an attendance register; students do not need the guest's home address or travel route.

Travel arrangements belong to the signed visit agreement. The office handbook does not promise a hotel, luggage storage or reimbursement for a missed train. Where a train delay affects the class, the host first gives participants a revised start time, then records the actual teaching minutes. The host must not invent a shorter lesson and mark it delivered at full length.

## Host handover example
For a Friday residency, Mara is the named studio host and Ivo is the visiting teacher. Mara opens the room, checks the register and keeps the emergency folder at the desk. Ivo introduces the artistic task. When an observer arrives, Mara explains where to sit and checks the visitor record. If the room is needed for a fire drill, both adults follow the building lead's instruction and the office later confirms any lost minutes. None of these operational roles decides which deposit is correct where the office handbook and welcome handout disagree.

## Cross-campus closing procedure

A host handover should tell the next adult what they need to do without filling a page with private details about the class. Start with the room and the time, then give the names of the adults who hold the key and the register. Note whether the guest has seen the exit route and knows where to find the first aid lead. Keep the music plan near the room notes so that a late change of device does not hold up the group. If the class shares a wall with a quiet activity, check the sound level from the hall before the students arrive. Tell the guest where to place a bag so that the door can open fully. A host who leaves for a short break must first tell the next host which students are present and whether anyone is due to arrive late. The next host should read back the room and group details to avoid a mistaken handover to a nearby class. Do not copy private phone numbers onto the public door sign. If a message needs to reach a guardian, use the office route and record the time it was sent. An artist may bring a paper plan for the lesson, but the host still keeps the studio register. A student's own note can explain a preferred cue, yet it does not replace the current support plan held by the office. When two rooms share a foyer, the host directs each group to the correct door rather than asking students to sort it out themselves. At the end of a session, allow time to check the room, collect lost items and tell the next teacher about any fault in the sound system. A worn cable is marked and set aside so that the next class does not discover the same fault by chance. The host must not unplug another room's working equipment to solve a local issue without speaking to that room's lead. If the artist needs a few more minutes to pack, move the conversation away from the class exit and keep the route clear. Students may ask for feedback at the desk, but the host should avoid a crowd forming around a guest who is trying to depart. A shared notebook can record the teaching theme and room layout while private student facts stay in the proper record. After the guest has left, check the floor for tape and return borrowed chairs to their marked places. The next host checks that the register folder is present before opening the room. Where the residency uses both the north and south buildings, the office compares the end of each room list with the next room's start list. This avoids a student being counted twice while walking between buildings. A late note should say what changed and who accepted the change. It should not erase the earlier entry or imply the previous host saw information that arrived later. The office keeps the two room sheets together for the end of day check. The closing host then follows the exact envelope rule at the end of this paragraph. For a guest residency spanning both buildings, the final host handover sheet must be sealed in the green envelope marked GUEST NORTH.

## Scheduling details that do not change the booking
A studio rehearsal led by a regular teacher remains a regular rehearsal even if a guest sits at the side to watch. The office should not create a second workshop charge solely because a visiting artist is in the building. Conversely, an advertised guest workshop is not quietly converted to an ordinary class when the guest is delayed. The host explains the change and the office offers the recorded choices. Printed room plans show the expected sequence of activities, but the teacher can shorten a warm-up when safety requires it without changing the named booking identity.

## Keeping separate records
The guest expense record, student register and workshop receipt serve different purposes. The expense record can contain a train reference; the register needs only the class participants and relevant support steps; the receipt records payment. A host should not attach one full record to another simply because it is easier than copying the necessary booking number. When a guest returns next term, use a new dated record and check the contact route again rather than treating last term's sign-in as continuing permission.
